details: European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel has advocated for central banks to move their money natively onto distributed ledger technology (DLT) to realize the full benefits of tokenization and safeguard financial stability. Speaking at the Bank of England's "Future of Money" conference, Schnabel presented three models for this integration: direct issuance of tokenized central bank reserves, bridging existing real-time gross settlement systems with DLT platforms, and using private intermediaries to issue tokens backed by central bank reserves. She stressed that stablecoins are complements, not substitutes, for central bank money, which must remain the ultimate settlement asset. The ECB is already advancing this shift through initiatives like Project Pontes.
title: ECB Calls for Central Banks to Adopt On-Chain Money

details: The US economy added a significantly lower-than-anticipated 29,000 nonfarm payroll jobs in September, with the unemployment rate rising to 4.2%. This figure fell short of economists' forecasts and followed downward revisions to job gains in July and August. Wage growth also slowed to 3.0% annually, its lowest in over five years. This weaker jobs report has led to a reduction in market expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, with the likelihood of an October rate increase decreasing. While the Fed's September hike was aimed at combating inflation, the slowing labor market suggests that further tightening might be reconsidered, easing pressure on risk assets.
title: US Adds Fewer Jobs Than Expected in September, Fed Hike Odds Decline
